items.weakness_text: No error bars are reported; How variable are the results? It would be good for the authors to present some sense of performance variation across tasks (e.g., 95% CIs around the mean; stdev, etc).
The phrasing of Program-to-Geometry in Section 3.1 is confusing; unclear whether Program-to-Geometry is a single task or two capabilities.
Clarify how their work relates to https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.08313, which seems quite similar, especially related to RQ1 (which was at ICLR last year and is not cited).
Incorporate evaluations using vision models that directly interpret the rendered images, alongside results from multimodal models, to serve as a reference baseline.

There is a discrepancy between Table 1 and the corresponding text on page 8: "For example, GPT-o1 drops from 76.02% to 43.35%, and DeepSeek-R1 drops from 75.27% to 40.38%." Please verify and ensure alignment between the visual and textual elements.

Provide a standardized definition of the dataset's input-output format, including an accessible, introductory explanation of Asymptote code to enhance clarity for readers unfamiliar with procedural drawing languages.
A more detailed analysis for the main results table in Section 5.3 is required; lacks insights (e.g., why angle and volume are not the most challenging questions for abstract?).
Add one most recent model for evaluation.
Discuss related work benchmarks such as SGPBench and SGP-GenBench in the discussion/related work sections.
The paper does not cite SGP-Bench (ICLR 2025), which evaluates LLMs’ understanding of symbolic graphics programs without rendering; should be discussed and contrasted.
GeoGramBench stays within Asymptote/Matplotlib-style code and contest-style numeric targets, limiting to the mathematical geometry domain, a fraction of the broad geometric spatial capability.
The final accuracy is inconclusive for the geo-spatial capability because the questions also involve mathematical reasoning.
DSL choice (Asymptote/Matplotlib) can significantly affect evaluation results; few-shot CoT experiments are important to justify the evaluation.
